retained_voice_results.650c326bf22713553b41640f250baeaba86b0389:
iOS voice: a simulator test for talking over the reply

-OAVoiceBarge (debug only) plays a second recording over the reply once it
has played 300 ms. The new UI test checks that playback is cut, frame
decisions are applied, and the new turn is recognized and answered. Passes
offline, live with echo and live with Gemini.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
retained_voice_results.31f990fa2572bc26a2cc20a16619d0532a797678:
iOS 1055: reply audio paced on the player's clock; the voice test listens like a phone

1054 queued every downlink buffer twice (once per callback type) and paced
on consumed callbacks, so replies stalled and played double. Playback now
schedules each buffer once and keeps 200 ms queued beyond what the player
has taken by its own clock, which doesn't lag by the output latency the way
played-back callbacks do. The reply caption only grows.

The simulator voice test now measures each reply as a listener hears it
(time to first audio, play time against audio length, gaps where the
player's clock runs past the audio, caption words lost), with a simulated
0.25 s phone output latency. 1054's code fails it (6749 ms to play 3200 ms,
168 gaps); this passes offline and live (Google speech, echo and Gemini).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
